episodes.199058: A compact upper level low pressure system tracked across New Mexico and West Texas from the morning to afternoon on the second. Strong forcing for ascent with this system combined with a dryline in the Rolling Plains and abundant instability generated isolated thunderstorms in the extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle into western Oklahoma. One of these storms became severe in eastern Childress County producing quarter size hail.
episodes.199104: A quick-moving/compact upper trough instigated scattered thunderstorm development across the Red River Valley during the afternoon and evening of the 2nd. Despite weak instability and modest wind shear, a pocket of cold temperatures aloft (i.e., steep lapse rates) facilitated the development of short-lived severe thunderstorms, yielding a few reports of hail across the aforementioned area.
